reply.text:
The error means the response JSON has no `carbohydrates` field. Common causes: the DTO lacks a public getter/property named `carbohydrates`, the mapper didn't set that field, Jackson renamed it, or the controller returned a different structure (e.g. an array or wrapper). Check the printed response body (you already call `.andDo(print())`) to see what was returned.

Quick fixes:
- Ensure `MealDto` has a `carbohydrates` field with a public getter (or `@JsonProperty("carbohydrates")`).
- Ensure your mapper sets `carbohydrates` on the mapped DTO.
- Ensure the controller returns the created `MealDto` (not `null` or a different payload).
- Use numeric expectations in the test (JSON numbers vs strings).

Example corrected test assertions (use numeric values):

```java
// java
@Test
@Transactional
public void testAddMeal() throws Exception {
    final MealDto mealDto = new MealDto("Chicken Salad", 400, 20, 30, 10);

    mvc.perform(post("/api/meals")
            .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
            .content(TestUtils.asJsonString(mealDto))
            .accept(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON))
        .andDo(print())
        .andExpect(status().isOk())
        .andExpect(jsonPath("$.name").value("Chicken Salad"))
        .andExpect(jsonPath("$.calories").value(400))
        .andExpect(jsonPath("$.carbohydrates").value(20))
        .andExpect(jsonPath("$.protein").value(30))
        .andExpect(jsonPath("$.fat").value(10));
}
```
